A1.justification: Both complete 20-page PDFs describe the same work and contain matching main text and Appendices A–L. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that the research content, equations, figures, and tables are identical; visible differences are confined to the first-page arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v3.pdf reports original model-training experiments, sparsity measurements, benchmark evaluations, and decoding-speed measurements in Sections 4–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4.pdf retains the same original training, sparsity, benchmark, and decoding experiments, including the detailed results in Tables 1–6 and Appendix L.

M1.justification: The model architecture, CETT-PPL-1% procedure, sparsity-stabilizing strategy, and binary-search algorithm are identical, including Appendices E–F.

E1.justification: The training and validation corpora, commonsense reasoning and reading comprehension tasks, and additional complex benchmarks remain identical in Appendices H and K.

E2.justification: The same comparators participate in each comparison: Straightforward ReLU, Top-k, FAT-ε, and CETT in Figures 2–3; MoE configurations versus the vanilla Transformer in Figure 12; and PowerInfer versus llama.cpp in Appendix L.

E3.justification: Model scales, training stages, benchmark shot counts and metrics, PPL tolerances, checkpoint selection, and the 100-prompt acceleration protocol are unchanged in Section 3 and the appendices.

E4.justification: Both versions contain identical analyses of activation functions, training-data amount, width-depth ratio, parameter scale, training-loss dynamics, and dataset-wise, token-wise, and layer-wise activation patterns.

E5.justification: Both versions present the same point estimates and fitted curves without reported seed counts, repeated-run error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The checkpoint-averaging and fitting procedures are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical tables and plotted results match. Both report the 2.4B model's 6.48% limit activation ratio in Table 2 and decoding speeds of 41.79 versus 10.23 tokens per second for PowerInfer versus llama.cpp in Appendix L.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, including the FFN and CETT definitions, power-law forms, and neuron-grouping derivation, are identical. The accompanying assumptions and mathematical reasoning are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about CETT-PPL-1%, empirical sparsity laws, architectural and training guidance, and the 2.4B model demonstration.

C2.justification: The neuron-specialization interpretation in Section 5.3 and the computation-cost and dataset-dependence limitations in Appendix A are identical. No substantive explanations or qualifications change.

D1.justification: Data descriptions, training hyperparameters, fitting instructions, hardware specifications, and acceleration implementation details remain unchanged. The code/checkpoint availability statement and associated links are also identical.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to MoE, weight pruning, and earlier activation-sparsity research are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 16 May 2025 to v4 dated 30 June 2025 and gains a link to the later version. The title, authors, prose, headings, and section/appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The updated vertical arXiv stamp is slightly repositioned on page 1. All figures, tables, captions, and the layout of the research content remain identical; pages 2–20 render identically.

improvement.justification: The later PDF retains identical scientific content, evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information, including all appendices. Updating, linking, and slightly repositioning the version stamp does not meaningfully affect the paper's overall quality.
